Thanks — quick mapping from the ops side to help the sync: 

Summary of billing paths we typically support (pros/cons):
- GCP Marketplace Private Offer: Helio buys through Google; benefits: single invoice via GCP, easier co-sell via Google sales. Cons: Google requires private offer configuration and there are timing windows for approval.
- Third-party SaaS listing (GCP Marketplace SaaS): Redwood handles billing and invoicing; benefits: more direct revenue recognition for Redwood, faster to iterate on pricing. Cons: requires Redwood to be the invoice owner and can complicate some reseller scenarios.
- Direct invoicing (Net-30): For larger strategic deals we can accept PO and invoice Helio directly.

Procurement checklist we recommend before listing release:
- PO template completed (attached by Helio)
- License term sheet signed (we've drafted v1 as attached)
- SOC 2 artefact confirmed and secure link provided
- SKU mapping & metering plan (I will draft a short mapping doc during the sync)
- Finance approval (Marcus Lin) and Legal redline window (3–5 business days typical)

Attachments: license-term-sheet-v1.docx, SOW-draft.docx

For the sync I can bring the SKU metering proposal and a suggested timeline (1-week SLA to config private offer after PO + signed terms). If Helio prefers private offer path, we should also identify a Named Contact at Google to speed the approve flow — Maria, do you have a GCP Marketplace contact?

Jonas
